title: Sep 26 Results + Sep 27 Preview: Solid Friday, Eyes on the Mets
summary: 9-4 record on Friday keeps the momentum rolling into a weekend matchup in D.C.

content.value:
## Friday's Numbers Tell the Story

Another day at the office, another winning record in the books. We went 9-4 on Friday's slate—nothing flashy, but the kind of steady performance that keeps you in the black over a long season. I've been doing this long enough to know that 69.2% accuracy is right where you want to be when September pennant races heat up.

## The Hits and Misses

The Dodgers-Giants call at 63% was our most confident pick of the day, and LA came through as expected. The Rays over the Phillies at 61% was another strong read—Tampa's been one of those teams that quietly does exactly what the numbers suggest all season long.

Where did we stumble? The Nationals couldn't hold serve at home against the Mets, the Jays fell short against the Reds, and frankly, I thought the Guardians had a better shot in Kansas City. The Red Sox missing at home to the Rockies stings a bit, but Colorado's been playing spoiler down the stretch. Sometimes the underdog bites back.

## Saturday's Featured Play: Mets Back in Washington

Here's the thing about the Mets—they just beat the Nationals on Friday, and now we're backing them again on Saturday. It's a lean pick at 51%, basically a coin flip with a slight edge, but there's context here that matters.

Sean Manaea takes the ball for New York, and he's been quietly reliable in the second half. On the other side, DJ Herz gets the nod for Washington. The young lefty has shown flashes, but consistency has been elusive. When you're facing a Mets lineup that's scrapping for October positioning, those inconsistencies get exploited.

## The Veteran's Take

I've seen enough September baseball to know that momentum is real, even if the math says it shouldn't be. The Mets came into D.C. and won Friday night, and they're hungry. The margin here is razor-thin—51% is essentially saying these teams are evenly matched—but I'll take the team with something to play for and the more established starter on the mound.

Is it a lock? Absolutely not. But it's the kind of edge that adds up over time. Saturday's slate is setting up nicely, and this Mets-Nationals rematch is where the model sees the cleanest advantage.

Let's make it another winning day. See you at first pitch.

author: Max
